title: helm: private values templating init hooks - fix upgrade/rollback ordering
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: During recent private cluster upgrades we observed flakiness in the Helm upgrade/rollback path for the redwood-private chart. Post-upgrade hooks that validate migrations were running before templated ConfigMaps/Secrets applied, which caused the chart to report failures and trigger rollbacks that could not complete cleanly. This PR reworks hook ordering and adds a small pre-upgrade backup job to ensure rollback can restore secrets/config if a post-upgrade validation fails. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce explicit hook weights and separate pre-upgrade and post-upgrade hook templates to ensure deterministic ordering; 2) Add init backup job template (templates/init-job-backup.yaml) to snapshot K8s secrets/configmaps used by the installer when the cluster runs with KMS enabled; 3) Expand values.schema.json to include optional "backup.enabled" and "hooks.weights" with validation and default values; 4) Add a minimal Helm integration test for upgrade->rollback and a helper function to assert resource ordering in CI; 5) Bump chart version and update README/upgrade notes. Checklist: - [x] Reproduced flaky behavior locally and in CI - [x] Added unit/helm-integration test (test/helm/upgrade-rollback/test-upgrade.sh) - [x] Updated values.schema.json with validation and documentation - [x] Bumped Chart.yaml patch version - [x] Ran helm lint and static templating checks - [x] Confirmed rollback succeeds in e2e canary (perf-canary) Notes for operators: - This change is backwards compatible: new values (backup.enabled, hooks.weights) default to off/standard ordering. Operators who relied on implicit hook ordering should not be impacted, but we recommend enabling backup.enabled=true for clusters with KMS-managed secrets during the next maintenance window. - If you have custom hook weights in your values, review the new hooks.weights keys and migrate to the documented names. Testing: Local helm unit tests and CI helm-integration test simulate an upgrade that triggers a validation failure; the pre-upgrade backup allows the post-upgrade rollback job to restore state. CI history: initial push failed helm-lint due to a templating edge-case in helper function; fixed in commit that updated _helpers.tpl. Merge: squash-merged after approvals.
